source: session finding (2026-08-11) from pipeline run-history review; promoted to a task by Erik via /work 2026-08-11
title: bronze_wgi fails intermittently with HTTP 502 on scheduled runs
description:
The bronze_wgi ingestion was reported failing with HTTP 502 on 2 of the last 5 scheduled runs (observed 2026-08-11). TREAT THAT COUNT AS UNVERIFIED — it was recorded in a dashboard note and has no durable measurement behind it in the repo. Re-measure the real failure rate from the pipeline run history before diagnosing anything.

Measurement contract (from project memory, the queryactivityruns API): there is no item id in the path, and the date window is MANDATORY — omit it and you get 200 with an empty body for every run, which reads exactly like 'no failures' and is the trap here. A negative finding about failure frequency needs a positive control: the same query must be shown returning a known-present run.

This is an intermittent upstream failure, so the discipline in .claude/rules/agents.md § 'Root Cause Over Symptom' applies with force. Establish WHERE the 502 originates before adding any retry: the World Bank API itself, the Fabric HTTP path, or the notebook's own request handling. A retry with backoff is a legitimate fix for a genuinely transient upstream 502 — it is NOT a legitimate fix for a malformed request, an auth expiry, or a rate limit, all of which can also surface as a 5xx and would be papered over by retrying.

Whatever the fix, a PERMANENT failure must still fail loudly. Do not let a bounded retry turn a real outage into a silent partial load — bronze_wgi feeding nothing means the governance half of gold_supply_risk degrades quietly, and the project already has one permanent governance gap (Taiwan) that must not be confused with an ingestion failure.

Do not commit or push. The deploy and the observation window over subsequent scheduled runs are Erik's half.
acceptanceCriteria: The actual failure rate is re-measured from pipeline run history over a stated date window, with a positive control proving the query returns rows at all. Report the real numbers even if they contradict the '2 of 5' claim.
The 502's origin is established — upstream API, Fabric HTTP path, or notebook request handling — with evidence, not inference. If the evidence is inconclusive, say so and stop rather than guessing.
The fix matches the diagnosis. If and only if the failure is a transient upstream 5xx, implement a bounded retry with backoff at the fetch.
A permanent failure still fails the run loudly. Demonstrate that an unrecoverable error is not swallowed and does not produce a silent partial load.
Any behaviour change is reflected in docs/epi_wgi_ingestion.md.
Erik's half: deploy, then confirm over subsequent scheduled runs that the failure no longer recurs (or that it now surfaces correctly if the cause was not transient).
notes:
Approved by Erik 2026-08-11 (out-of-spec gate) as one of three confirmed defects that had no task behind them.

The reported '2 of the last 5 scheduled runs' is the weakest evidence of the three defects — it is a session observation with no artifact in the repo backing it, which is why AC1 makes re-measurement the first deliverable rather than an assumption. If re-measurement shows the failure is gone or was misattributed, an honest null result closes this task; do not manufacture a fix for a problem that is not there.

Relevant hazard from project memory: bronze writes of source CSVs crash at saveAsTable on column names containing spaces (DELTA_INVALID_CHARACTERS_IN_COLUMN_NAMES), and local Spark never invokes a Delta writer, so that class of failure is invisible locally. A 502 is not that failure mode, but if the run history shows a DIFFERENT error alongside the 502s, check for it.

---

[IMPLEMENTATION 2026-08-13] [Multi-file: 5 files modified] NOT a null result — the defect is real, and the reported count was accurate. AC1 (re-measurement, with positive control): queried all 70 pipeline run instances via POST /v1/workspaces/{ws}/datapipelines/pipelineruns/{runId}/queryactivityruns with the mandatory wide date window. Of the 9 SCHEDULED runs since the 06:00 schedule went live (2026-08-05 20:20 test firing → 2026-08-13), bronze_wgi failed the run on 2: a80a0c3c (2026-08-07) and 7e3f55df (2026-08-09) = 2/9. The dashboard's '2 of the last 5' was CORRECT as recorded on 2026-08-11 — the last 5 scheduled runs at that moment were 08-07..08-11, containing exactly those 2 failures. As of implementation the 4 most recent scheduled runs (08-10..08-13) are all green, so the rate is episodic, not steady. POSITIVE CONTROL (explicitly observed, both directions): the same call WITH the window returns 10 activity rows for green run 498f7b5e and 9 for failed run 7e3f55df; WITHOUT the window it returns HTTP 200 + 0 rows for BOTH — the documented empty-200 trap reproduced, so the 'no failures' reading is provably distinguishable from a broken probe.

AC2 (origin, by evidence not inference): UPSTREAM — api.worldbank.org's gateway. Three independent lines. (1) bronze_wgi is a Notebook activity issuing a direct requests.get from the Spark driver; there is no Fabric HTTP connector/Copy activity anywhere in the path, so the 502 is the status line the upstream returned to raise_for_status(). The captured error string names the upstream URL verbatim: 'World Bank API call failed for GOV_WGI_PV.EST (page 3) after 5 attempts: 502 Server Error: Bad Gateway for url: https://api.worldbank.org/v2/...'. (2) The failing request is well-formed — replayed the exact failing URL (PV.EST page 3) live: HTTP 200 in 3.2s, pages=6, total=5400; a 40-request burst across all 6 indicators returned 40x 200, none slower than 10s. (3) The failing indicator/page DIFFERS per attempt (PV p3, CC p3, PV p3 on 08-09; GE p1, RQ p5, GE p1 on 08-07) — a malformed request would fail deterministically on the same page. Ruled out the three impostor causes the task warned about: auth expiry is impossible (World Bank Open Data is unauthenticated); malformed request cannot present as 5xx because this API reports bad input IN-BAND as HTTP 200 with a one-element error body (probed live with a bogus indicator code); rate limiting would be 429 and none was ever observed. So a 5xx from this host is necessarily gateway/infrastructure level = genuinely transient, which is what makes a retry the correct fix here rather than a paper-over.

AC3 (fix matches diagnosis): the notebook ALREADY had bounded retry+backoff from task-050 — the real defects were that it retried indiscriminately and its budget was too small. Added is_transient_request_error() classifying BEFORE any retry: 5xx and 429 transient, timeout/connection-reset/truncated-body transient, every other 4xx PERMANENT and raised immediately with a distinct message (previously a 404 would burn the full backoff budget and then be reported as an exhausted-retry outage — exactly the misdiagnosis the task warned against). Added retry_delay() honouring Retry-After. Widened the budget 5→8 attempts and cap 60→120s (5+10+20+40+80+120+120 = 395s ≈ 6.6 min per request, hard-bounded) — justified by measurement: on 08-07 attempt 2 ran 41 MINUTES and reached the 5th of 6 indicators, so most requests were succeeding throughout the degraded window and isolated 502s were each killing the whole run inside 75s.

AC4 (permanent failure still fails loudly, no silent partial load): verified the existing loud path live — on failed run 7e3f55df the activity list contains only 7 activities and bronze_to_silver_cleaning / silver_to_gold / data_quality_checks are ABSENT, i.e. the RuntimeError failed the activity and halted the pipeline. But demonstrating this uncovered a genuine silent-partial-load hole: fetch_indicator had two break-on-anomaly paths (unexpected body shape, null record set) that exited pagination, returned whatever had accumulated, and let the run go GREEN over a mode('overwrite') write that destroys the good snapshot. That path is REACHABLE (the in-band 200 error body is exactly what an invalid indicator code returns, and the World Bank already re-coded WGI once, 2026-07-26, classic CC.EST → GOV_WGI_CC.EST). Closed with four guards — in-band 200 error raises, null record set raises, pagination completeness checked against the API's own declared total per indicator, and an all-6-indicators check immediately before the overwrite. Guard 4 is load-bearing because bronze_wgi's DQ row-count band is 50..500,000, so losing a whole indicator (~5,000 of ~31,000 rows) sails through the DQ layer undetected — spun off as task-073.

AC5: docs/epi_wgi_ingestion.md gains a 'Failure Handling in bronze_ingest_wgi' section (measured rate, origin evidence, retry-policy table, the four guards, why the DQ band would not have caught it).

SELF-REVIEW: notebook AST-parses clean; 6 CELL / 7 METADATA markers intact and 0 PARAMETERS CELL markers (correct — the pipeline passes NO parameters to bronze_wgi, unlike bronze_epi — the misleading comment implying otherwise spun off as task-072). Ran the EDITED notebook's own fetch_indicator against the live API: PV.EST returned 5214 records across all 6 pages in 50.7s with the completeness check passing — happy path unregressed — and the bogus-indicator call raised as required. New tests/test_wgi_retry.py adds 29 assertions extracting the notebook's own functions via ast under the existing reference-implementation contract; both key tests genuinely fail against the old code. Full suite 329 passed (was 300). Nothing committed or pushed — HEAD is still 49e7c28 and all changes are working-tree only.

DECISION RECORDED: DEC-017 documents the choice of classified-retry-plus-guards over a 'keep-last-good-snapshot' alternative (which would trade away the loud-failure requirement this task explicitly demands) — see decision-017-bronze-wgi-upstream-502-policy.md.

FOLLOW-UP TASKS SPUN OFF (both pending Erik's out-of-spec approval): task-072 (misleading parameters-cell comment) and task-073 (DQ row-count band too wide to catch a lost indicator, defense-in-depth on top of this task's ingest-side guard).

ISSUE FLAGGED FOR HUMAN (not actioned): WGI is annual data but re-fetched and overwritten daily, so a transient upstream outage fails a pipeline that had no new data to collect — a 'keep last good snapshot' policy would make this non-fatal but trades away the loud-failure requirement AC4 demands; recorded as DEC-017's declined Option B, Erik's call to revisit if nuisance failures become a real problem.

AZ CLI RECIPE (for any future Fabric/Azure REST work on this machine — homebrew's az is broken, was NOT touched): PYTHONPATH=/opt/homebrew/Cellar/azure-cli/2.72.0/libexec/lib/python3.12/site-packages uv run --no-project --python 3.12 python -c "from azure.cli.core import get_default_cli; get_default_cli().invoke(['account','show','--output','json'])" — the uv-managed CPython 3.12.13 is ABI-compatible with the Cellar's cpython-312-darwin .so files. GOTCHA: az writes to the real stdout fd, so contextlib.redirect_stdout does NOT capture it and will leak the bearer token into a transcript — capture with cli.invoke([...], out_file=io.StringIO()) instead. Third independent rediscovery of this workaround across task-065's implementer, task-065's verifier, and this task's implementer — worth promoting into root ./CLAUDE.md's Gotchas section.

POSITIVE CONTROL, both directions, on both a green and a failed run: WITH the mandatory date window the call returns 10 rows and 9 rows respectively; WITHOUT the window it returns HTTP 200 with 0 rows for BOTH — the documented empty-200 trap reproduced.

AC2 ORIGIN (checked, not inferred). No Fabric HTTP connector in the WGI path: bronze_wgi is type TridentNotebook (retry=2, timeout 12h); the string 'worldbank' appears 0 times in the entire pipeline definition (positive control: same probe found 2 HttpServer and 4 Copy occurrences elsewhere, so the probe works). Error string matches the code exactly: pulled the full activity error message and extracted the verbatim pre-change format string. Per-attempt failing-page sequence confirmed directly from the API. The 41-minute claim measured: 40.7 min. Re-probed the live upstream: the exact failing URL now returns HTTP 200 in 0.18s; the bogus-indicator probe returns HTTP 200 with the in-band error body — confirming first-hand the premise the retry policy rests on.

AC3 CLASSIFIER (traced, not read). is_transient_request_error: 429 or 500<=s<=599 -> True; all other statuses -> False; no response -> True only for Timeout/ConnectionError/ChunkedEncodingError, else False (fails closed). Negative control against HEAD: old code made 5 calls and slept [5,10,20,40] on a permanent 404, reporting it as exhausted-retry; new code makes 1 call, raises immediately with a distinct PERMANENT message.

AC4 GUARDS (all four present, structurally sound, absence in old code demonstrated). Negative control against HEAD: in-band 200 error, null record set, and short pagination all SILENTLY returned partial/empty data in the old code; all three now raise. Guard 4 sits before the mode('overwrite') write, confirmed by reading AND by executing the guard logic in isolation (5-of-6 blocks, 6-of-6 proceeds). Loud-failure path confirmed live: both failed runs show only 7 distinct activities with bronze_to_silver_cleaning/silver_to_gold/data_quality_checks absent.
